---
title: "Shortlists"
subtitle: "Collect candidates as you work, then turn them into a report"
---

The **shortlist** is where you gather the iBGCs worth keeping. It accumulates across everything you do — filtering, searching, comparing — and is the bridge to the [report](report.qmd) and its downloads. It is the platform's main output: the set of candidates you carry into the lab.

## Adding iBGCs

- **Right-click → Add to shortlist** on any iBGC, in the [roster](bgc-roster.qmd), on a [map](umap.qmd), or in a [detail panel](ibgc-detail.qmd).
- **Add all to shortlist** in the roster footer adds every iBGC matching the current query at once.

The shortlist holds up to **1,000 iBGCs**. If a bulk add would exceed the cap, the platform adds what it can and tells you how many were skipped; if the query matched more than were considered, it notes that too, so you know the selection was truncated.

## Where it lives

The shortlist is stored **in your browser**, so it persists between sessions on the same machine and stays available no matter which result tab or search you use. It is not sent to the server until you explicitly generate a report or export.

You can review the shortlist, remove individual entries, or clear it from the shortlist control in the discovery platform header.

## Turning a shortlist into a report

When you are ready, click **Generate Report**. The platform sends your selected iBGC ids to the server, materialises a full summary, and opens the [report page](report.qmd). The report has a stable link (a token in the URL) you can bookmark or share; it stays available for a period after generation, after which you can generate it again from the same shortlist.

## A typical session

1. Filter and search to surface candidates.
2. Add the good ones to the shortlist as you inspect them.
3. Refine — add more from a different query, remove ones that don't hold up.
4. **Generate Report** and download GenBank files and tables for your top set.
